style: Flat matte South Indian temple mural; broad opaque mineral color fields, firm dark contours, shallow decorative space, restrained painted ornament. No glossy gold, 3D drift, readable text, signatures, logos or watermarks.

scenes.1: Durvasa, Indra and Airavata each appear once with their ordinary contracted anatomy; the fallen garland links the curse and crushed flowers.
scenes.2: Vishnu has four arms; Brahma has four total heads and four arms; Shiva and Indra keep ordinary two-arm forms; devas remain distinct.
scenes.3: Vishnu has four attached arms and teaches a distinct small deva group.
scenes.4: Vishnu has four arms; Garuda has one head, two wings and two legs; devas and asuras remain distinct ordinary humanoids.
scenes.5: Vasuki is one continuous serpent; asuras hold the single head end and devas hold the tapering tail end.
scenes.6: Kurma is a complete tortoise with four legs and one shell directly supporting Mandara; no human torso or arms.
scenes.7: Kurma remains a complete tortoise while lifting Mandara from below.
scenes.8: Vasuki remains one continuous serpent with head and tail held by the correct groups; no second Vishnu figure.
scenes.9: Vishnu has four arms; Brahma has four total heads and four arms; Shiva and devas remain distinct.
scenes.10: Poison fumes travel from Vasuki’s single head toward the asuras; rain falls only over devas; no Vishnu figure.
scenes.11: Vishnu has exactly two arms, both gripping the same continuous Vasuki; Bhattathiri is a secondary prayerful witness.
